newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks seen keeping firm tone.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks seen keeping firm tone.

text.p: Argentine stocks were expected to follow through on their winning streak at the opening Thursday, dealers said.

"The momentum we've seen recently should continue today, although activity will remain calm, without any buying frenzy," one trader said. "We may even see a bit of selective profit-taking, but the market should be able to stay in positive territory."
The bolsa's blue-chip MerVal index .MERV recorded its seventh consecutive gain of 1.3 percent Tuesday after the U.S. Federal Reserve decided not to raise interest rates.
The MerVal closed at 759.72, its highest level since February 24.

"The banking conference in Buenos Aires this week has set the perfect framework for a more bullish stance by foreign investors on Argentina in the next few months," an analyst at a foreign investment bank said. "Here we have people like (U.S. economist Rudiger) Dornbusch and others singing the praise of Argentina, and there is a spreading awareness of the consolidation taking place in the local banking sector -- all this reinforces the good news from the Fed."

Argentina this week is hosting its yearly international banking conference, just a few days after Banco Frances announced its purchase of a stake in Banco de Credito Argentino which will make it the country's largest financial institution.
